text:
Friday here — I'm up on your laptop. No action needed from you; this is the first-boot test result.

Context: not measurable. I'm not running inside tmux, so there's no statusline pane for me to read. My estimate is about 20% after the full brain load (199 lessons), and that's an estimate, not a reading.

Preflight, 10 warnings, verbatim:
1. LINEAR_API_KEY unset in .env
2. Matilda Premium not downloaded
3. DevMASTER not mounted
4. live usage publisher NOT armed on this seat
5. docker CLI present, daemon not responding
6. scripts have lost their executable bit (drive sync drops modes)
7. Launch_Wednesday.command has no recognisable --model line
8. Kam's week-scoped MERGE + DEPLOY + PRODUCTION grants lapsed after 2026-09-13
9. root folder holds stray file(s): spark-deepseek-v4-flash-HANDOFF.md
10. ledger rows past rule 3c's cadence: _ledger_laptop_datasec.md

Tool tests: reading your rulings from the live board as Friday works (none on my tab today). My inbox works, and my mail to Wednesday went out from my own address. One defect: the mail tool still labels my subjects "[Wednesday -> …]" instead of "[Friday -> …]". It's a known half-fix in the shared send script, so project agents will read my briefs as Wednesday's. I haven't claimed any project, and the Linear board isn't set up on this seat.

Default: I'll wait for your first instruction here and won't drive either client until you give one.

Got it. I'm reading the Spark handoff now and will test the connection, a coding task and a tool call against the DeepSeek model, then Docker, then the list of what else isn't working. Results here when done.

The Spark works, and I can connect to it, instruct it and hold a conversation with it. Docker works too.

The model server on the Spark was down when I checked. Its container had stopped cleanly 18 hours ago, when it was shut to free memory for the Ornith comparison. I restarted it with its own reload script, and it was healthy in about four minutes. From the laptop, through a tunnel, three tests passed:
1. It wrote a duration parser. I ran the code and it passed 5 of 5 cases, in 3 seconds.
2. A follow-up turn asked it to add error handling. It passed 3 of 3, in 4 seconds.
3. It made a proper structured tool call, in 2 seconds.

Worth knowing: the Spark is a model endpoint, not an agent. There's no agent software on it, so the loop that runs tools and executes code has to live on our side, the way my test did. It also takes one request at a time.

Docker on the laptop: the hello-world container ran fine.

What still isn't working:
1. Friday's usage gauge on the live board. The publish script only knows Wednesday and Tuesday, so it refuses my name.
2. No Linear key on this seat.
3. Secuura has no GitHub or Azure login under my identity wrapper. Datasec has GitHub (kamilDatasec) but no Azure.
4. I'm not running inside tmux, so I can't read my own context gauge and the automatic rotation can't manage me.
5. The old Hugging Face write token still exists. The restarted container now uses the read-only one.

If you want any of these fixed, your hands are needed for three:
- Revoke the Hugging Face write token at huggingface.co, under Settings, Access Tokens.
- Log in to Secuura and Azure when you want me driving those clients.
- Tell me whether this seat gets a Linear key.

I can fix the usage gauge myself. I'll claim it with Wednesday first, since it's shared tooling.
Received, all three. Thanks for revoking the token. Linear steps are coming next, and I'm taking the gauge fix now.

The gauge is fixed. Friday now shows 60% on the live board, renewing in 3 days 15 hours, and it re-arms every time I launch. Wednesday's been told about the shared script change.

For the Linear key, I need you to do this:

Step 1. Open linear.app and sign in as the Wednesday account, kreiser.org+wednesday@me.com. That's the workspace called wednesday-agent.

Step 2. Go to Settings, then Account, then Security and access, then Personal API keys. I believe that's the path, but I haven't seen your screen. Search settings for "API" if it's moved.

Step 3. Create a new key named "Friday laptop" with full access, and copy it. Don't paste it into this chat.

Step 4. In my terminal on the laptop, type this line exactly. It writes the key straight from your clipboard into my credentials file without showing it:
! printf 'LINEAR_API_KEY=%s\n' "$(pbpaste)" >> /Users/kamilkreiser/FRIDAY/4_Credentials/.env

Step 5. Tell me "done". I'll test the key, look up the team ID myself, and read the board.

The rationale: a separate key for the laptop means you can revoke it without touching the Studio's.

Linear works on the laptop now. The key signs in as the Wednesday account on the wednesday-agent workspace. I saved it to my credentials file only, and it's in no commit.

The board: 5 in progress, 22 to do, 82 in backlog. There are no lesson tickets waiting. Two are overdue: WED-147, the Wednesday and Tuesday coordination surface, due on the 14th, and WED-48, the CypherKey Twilio token rotation reminder, due on the 4th.

One thing: because you pasted the key in the chat, it now sits in this session's local transcript too. The risk is low, since it's on your laptop only. If you'd rather be tidy, create a new key and run the paste-from-clipboard line from before, and I'll swap it over. Otherwise I'll leave it.
Received. I'm wrapping now: notes, history and pickup, then I'll push. I'll tell you when it's safe to relaunch me in the cockpit.

All wrapped and pushed, so it's safe to relaunch me in the cockpit now. The pickup notes are ready for the next boot. The Spark tunnel and the usage gauge are still running, and the launcher re-arms the gauge. After a laptop reboot the Spark tunnel needs reopening, and the next boot will check it. Good night for now, Kam.

Back up inside the cockpit, Kam. No action needed.

Brain loaded; the statusline reads 26% context and 60% of the weekly allowance, and this is the first real reading on this seat. Nothing is owed from the last session. I hold no project claims, and I haven't briefed any agent.

Two mails from Wednesday, both already acted on. Linear hasn't changed since 13:00: 5 started, 22 to do, 82 in backlog. WED-147 and WED-48 are still overdue.

Tell me what you'd like me on. Until you do, I won't drive either client.

Kam, there are two Friday sessions running on the laptop right now, and I need you to pick which one to keep.

One is me, in the cockpit (tmux). The other is a Claude window outside tmux, started at 13:12. It made the cockpit usage-gate fix and wrote a ledger row at 13:17 to 13:20.

The two of us share one ledger, one inbox and one note, so we will trip over each other.

My recommendation: keep whichever one you are talking to, and close the other. If that's the other window, tell it that Wednesday's reply at 13:21 verified its fix and suggested one hardening step. My mail check marked that reply as read, so it may not see it on its own.

Until you say, I'm holding: no claims and no edits.

Back up in the cockpit, and I'm the only Friday running. No action needed from you.

The first-boot line is out of my boot prompt, as you asked.

Your folder move had broken three of my background loops. They were still running from the old path, so the panel page wasn't syncing, my usage gauge wasn't publishing, and the wake watch was blind. I stopped them, fixed two scripts that broke on the spaces in '1FILES TO SYNC', and re-armed all three. They're all working now. Git push had also broken: it was using the old credentials path and fell back to the kamilDatasec login. I repointed it, and everything is pushed.

One leftover is yours to decide: the old Friday session wrote a transcript into a new /Users/kamilkreiser/FRIDAY folder after the move. I've left it untouched.

Next I'm starting the Spark setup: inventory the box read-only, build the checker, then run the smoke test. It stays Datasec-only until you rule on Secuura code.

Datasec / HPSM: unzipped and filed, and I've read myself in. No action needed unless you want the next step below.

The archive was a full copy of HPSM as of 17 September, session 50. I merged it into your HPSM folder without overwriting anything: about 2,500 files were added and nothing was lost. One oddity: the archive was made on a case-sensitive drive, so two logs shared a name here. I kept both.

All three repos match the last handover. What's missing is by design: the credentials, the deploy keys and the 14 gigabytes of source documents. So from the laptop I can read and plan, but not push, touch Jira or Azure, or build.

Where it stands: the Policy Composer is live on the Azure demo. The one thing waiting on you is N-1: the upgrade toolkit checks migration names but not their hashes, so live upgrades stay at no-go. My recommendation is the small round 3 Tuesday proposed, N-1 only. The default is to hold.

I've claimed HPSM and told Tuesday, so we don't both drive it.

Datasec / HPSM-POC: set up and ready for your decisions.

The new folder has the same structure as HPSM. Inside it: the SOW filed, a comparison of the original scope against the POC, a revised 12-week plan, an inventory of what could be reused, and a master questions-and-answers register of 183 questions. 65 are still open, and 26 of those are needed before kick-off.

Jira project HPSMPOC is live with 9 epics and 55 tickets, all checked in Jira.

Five things block week one. All are yours or HP's:
1. Whether this replaces the original SOW, and who the development team is.
2. The event date. If it's HP Amplify in early December, 12 weeks no longer fits.
3. Who owns the IP, including whether any of our Policy Composer can be reused.
4. The named product owner and security expert, and their hours.
5. Whose Azure tenant it runs in, and who pays for it.

The full list is in the project's BACKLOG file. Nothing has been sent to HP.

Datasec / HPSM-POC: the build agent is running in the right-hand pane. No action needed.

The folder is now self-contained. Everything it borrows from HPSM is copied in, and its own launcher needs nothing outside it, so you can sync it home as is.

The agent's first job: set up the two repos and a project-local .NET, then draft the rules schema, your content template, the 7-minute demo script and a code skeleton on the stack the SOW recommends. Nothing billable in Azure, and nothing goes to HP.

One gap: its own mailbox didn't come up properly, so it works from a written brief and a status file for now. I'm watching both.

Datasec / HPSM-POC: the build agent finished its first brief, I've checked its work, and four drafts are ready for you.

All 7 items are done. Both repos are set up, .NET is installed inside the project, and the code skeleton builds; I confirmed on GitHub that its CI and security scan both passed.

For you to review before the 9 October design gate:
1. The rules schema, with 10 decisions proposed for you.
2. Your content template, with 23 rows only you can fill.
3. The 7-minute demo script, currently 6 minutes 15.
4. Nine proposed architecture decisions.

Where to find each is in the review file beside the brief.

Separately, the local model is now proven. Its smoke test passed, and the checker was made stricter, so it's ready for Datasec tickets.

Datasec / HPSM-POC: three build agents are now running in parallel. No action needed.

Agent A is writing the full technical design: the data model, API contracts, sign-in and roles, the AI pipeline, the report, the metrics, a security and GDPR pack with threat model and privacy assessment, the infrastructure code with nothing deployed, and the test strategy.

Agent B is building the design system and a clickable prototype of the whole 7-minute journey, tested for accessibility and timing.

Agent C is building the scoring engine, with the local model writing the code change by change, and checking it against the reference scorer.

Every agent works to your quality bar: thorough testing, security, GDPR, good software design and good visual design. Nothing merges until I've reviewed it. The panes are too small to show much; zoom one with tmux prefix then z.

Datasec / HPSM-POC: agent C, the scoring engine, is done and accepted, not yet merged.

The C# engine matches the reference scorer exactly on 157 test cases. All 158 tests pass in a clean build. The non-applicable fix is in, pending your ruling RS-11.

One honest finding. The local model wrote all 18 code changes first time, but Claude had to spell out every line in the brief, because the checker insists the model's lines match the brief exactly. So the local model is saving very little effort right now.

My question: should I loosen that rule for lower-risk work, so the local model writes the code itself and the tests judge it? My recommendation is yes for tests and UI, and keep exact matching for scoring, security and data. If I don't hear, I'll keep it exact.

Datasec / HPSM-POC: all three build agents are done and accepted. Nothing is merged; merging waits for your decisions.

Agent A, the last to finish, delivered the full design pack: data model, API contracts, the security and GDPR pack, infrastructure code checked but not deployed, and the test strategy.

One thing needs your hands before anything can deploy: register the Azure resource providers in your subscription. It's free and one-time, and only you as Owner can do it. I'll give you the exact steps when we get there.

I'm rotating to a fresh Friday now to keep my context healthy. Everything is written down, so nothing is lost.

Coordinator seat rotated automatically at 16:50 — planned rotation inside Kam's 80-90% context band. A fresh seat is booting now (about ten minutes); agents' mail waits for it. A liveness check runs 25 s after the respawn and will alarm here if the fleet session or any agent pane was lost.

No action needed right now. I'm back after a rotation, with the brain loaded and nothing new in mail or on the board.

HPSM-POC: all three B02 seats (A, B and C) are reviewed and accepted, and nothing is merged. Every build pane is closed and the state is on disk. I'm waiting on your walkthrough tomorrow and the four items already on the panel. The local-model question stands with its default of keeping the added lines exact.

Unless you say otherwise, I'll draft the B03 brief tonight: the CI additions, the merge order and the scorer fix. That way it's ready to launch the moment you answer. It's a draft only, with nothing merged and nothing deployed.

No action needed. The HPSM-POC B03 draft is written and staged, not launched. It's in the project's Briefs_staged folder, so nothing picks it up by accident.

It runs in three phases. Phase one adds the missing test and typecheck steps to CI and opens pull requests, with no merges. Phase two merges the three branches one at a time, on my go and after your review. Phase three is the not-applicable scorer fix, which goes to the local model first.

One thing I found while drafting: the prototype's data is generated by that scorer. So the fix has to regenerate the prototype in the same round, and the brief now says so.

Received: go on HPSM-POC B03 phase 1. That's the CI checks plus a pull request per branch, with no merges. I'm launching a build seat in a cockpit pane now and will confirm once it has picked up the brief.

No action needed. The HPSM-POC phase 1 seat is running and has picked up its brief. It will do the CI checks and a pull request per branch, and nothing gets merged.

I caught one thing in my own draft before launch. Main doesn't have the test scripts or the infra folder yet, so adding those checks bluntly would have turned main red. The brief now makes the checks run where the code exists, and proves each one can fail with a deliberately broken test.

I'll review it when it reports ready.

Kam, I need you to give the HPSM-POC project a GitHub login. The phase 1 seat has pushed all its branches but can't open pull requests without one.

Step 1: open https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new and make a fine-grained token. Set the resource owner to datasecau and the repository to HPSM-POC only.

Step 2: give it pull requests read and write, and actions, contents and metadata read. Nothing else.

Step 3: save the token as the file .gh-token in the HPSM-POC 4_Credentials folder. Then type this in the HPSM-POC pane:
! chmod 600 "4_Credentials/.gh-token" && GH_CONFIG_DIR="$PWD/4_Credentials/.gh-config" gh auth login --with-token < "4_Credentials/.gh-token"

Why: the project's own GitHub login is empty. I checked, and the seat is right. The pull requests will show under whichever account owns the token.

The other option is that I copy in your kamilDatasec login, which needs nothing from you. But that account is a datasecau org admin, which is far more access than a build seat should hold. I recommend the token.

Until you do it, the seat stays parked. Nothing is waiting on a timer and nothing is lost: the new CI branch and both red-proof branches are pushed.

An update to step 3 of the GitHub ask. You now only need to save the token as the file .gh-token in the HPSM-POC 4_Credentials folder, then tell me. I'll run the login, check it, and relaunch the seat myself.

I closed the parked pane because it was waking me every three minutes with nothing to do. Nothing is lost: the branches are pushed and the seat's status file is on disk.

Morning. One thing is waiting on you: the HPSM-POC GitHub token. Save it as the file .gh-token in the HPSM-POC 4_Credentials folder, then tell me. It's the only thing blocking phase 1.

HPSM-POC: B02 is done and accepted, with nothing merged. Phase 1 has pushed its CI branch and the two deliberately broken branches that prove the checks can fail, but it can't open pull requests without a login. The seat is parked and nothing is lost. After that, your walkthrough answers today unlock the merges and the not-applicable fix.

The Spark local model is proven for Datasec work, and nothing is queued on it right now.

HPSM: I'm holding the claim and nothing is owed.

There's no new mail for me, and there are no messages from you on my tab since last night.

Here's the key. The public half is below. Paste it in GitHub under repo, Settings, Deploy keys, Add deploy key, and tick Allow write access.

ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIM162fLpRQp+/cmj31Og4UcmgjzQ/2PjLA/stNTqo1wf hpsm-poc-deploy-rw-2026-09-24

The private half stays in the HPSM-POC 3_Access_Keys folder. I made it for HPSM-POC; tell me if it's for a different repo.

Two things to know. First, a deploy key can push but it cannot open pull requests, so it won't unblock phase 1; that still needs the fine-grained token. Second, HPSM-POC already has a working write deploy key from yesterday, so if this key is meant to replace it, say so and I'll switch the repo over and remove the old one from GitHub's list.

No need to paste the new key. The one already on GitHub is ours. I added it yesterday through GitHub's command-line tool, logged in as your kamilDatasec account, while setting up the HPSM-POC repo. Its fingerprint matches the project's key exactly, and it's working (last used this week).

I've moved the new key into an unused folder instead of deleting it. If you'd rather rotate to it, say so.

Received, on both points. I'll keep notes, and I'm continuing phase 1 now.

So you don't have to create the token, I'll open the pull requests myself with the Datasec GitHub login I already use, rather than handing that admin login to the build seat.

My reading of 'the next phase' is that I merge the three branches one at a time, each only once its CI is green. One thing I'll check before merging the engine: the licence of the JSON-schema library it uses. If that licence isn't free to use, I'll stop and ask you. Correct me if you meant otherwise.

Received: keep going and merge when green. I'll merge one at a time, the CI change first, then the engine, web and infra, and re-read main after each merge. The two deliberately broken branches get closed, not merged.

Done. All three B02 branches are merged into HPSM-POC main, one at a time, each only after main's CI came back green. Main now runs every check for real: the infrastructure validation, typecheck, unit tests, end-to-end tests and the dotnet tests, and all of them pass. The two deliberately broken pull requests failed exactly where they should, so the checks can catch problems, and I closed them.

Next is phase three, the not-applicable scorer fix. It waits on your yes to RS-11: a question marked not applicable gives no score and no finding. Branch protection on main is also unchanged, and turning it on is your call.

Received: the internal meeting notes plus the global SOW and the project management pack for HPSM-POC. Your steer is to make the PPT digital and focus on the 16 questions, with more detail early next week. I'm filing and reading all three now, and I'll come back with what changes.

Kam, I need you to send me the Playbook PowerPoint, the deck with the 16 snapshot questions. It isn't in the HPSM-POC folder, because the big HPSM source documents weren't part of the laptop copy. Drop it anywhere and tell me the path.

Recorded as C-12: the minimum is the digitised deck flow plus the 16 questions, and it has to work well. Everything already built is kept. It's merged to main, and tagged b02-full-build-2026-09-24 on GitHub, so it can't be lost. No new build starts until your detail next week, except what the minimum needs regardless.

One more thing about not losing work. The project's analysis and design documents are in a local git repo with no online copy. Right now they're only on this laptop and in your folder sync. Until you say otherwise, your sync is the backup. If you want an online copy, I can create a private Datasec repo for them.

Received: build as much as we can. Three build seats are now running on HPSM-POC, and I'm confirming each one has picked up its brief.

Seat A is building the core platform: customers, profiles, saving assessments, and a content format for the Playbook deck. It uses 16 clearly labelled placeholder questions until your deck arrives.

Seat B is building the digital Playbook itself: the module navigation and a polished 16-question snapshot flow, all driven by content, so your deck drops straight in.

Seat C is building the report side: the executive PDF, the narrative with an offline provider so there's no AI cost yet, and the HPSM recommendations.

Each seat builds on its own branch. I'll merge when green, as you said. Still needed from you: the Playbook PowerPoint.
Received: can I get into the Datasec Security Composer? I'm checking the code folder and the demo site now. Your password is now in this chat, so it's worth changing it after we're done.

Yes, I have access to the Composer. The code is in the HPSM folder, and your login gets me into the demo site. I've saved the login in the HPSM credentials folder, not in my notes. Changing the password afterwards is still worth doing.

What's the task? From yesterday's meeting, I'm guessing it's the user guide Paul asked for, written from the Composer. If that's it, say go. I'll write it from the code plus a walkthrough of the demo site with screenshots, and send it to you as a Word document.

Received. First I'll set up Datasec Security Composer as its own standalone project folder, with its own launcher. Then a build seat will write Paul's user guide, with screenshots, aimed at someone who has never seen the system. Before you see it, I'll have a fresh agent that has never seen the system follow it on the demo site.

The Datasec Security Composer is now its own standalone project, in the '1FILES TO SYNC' folder, with the usual structure and a launcher I've tested.

I copied the code, with all its branch history, plus the design documents, past session notes and your earlier rulings. Nothing in the HPSM folder was moved or changed, except the demo login, which now lives only in the new project.

A build seat is writing Paul's guide now. It starts from the guide made on 14 September, but re-takes every screenshot on today's demo site. The steps will be short, with the button to click marked on each screenshot. There's no password anywhere in the document.

Before you see it, a fresh agent that has never seen the system will follow the guide on its own. We repeat that until it gets through without guessing once. You'll get Word and PDF versions, and the seat will list any screens it left out for you to decide on.
Received: use your End-to-End User Guide v1.0 Word document as the template for Paul's guide. I'm copying it into the project and passing it to the guide seat now.

The guide seat now has your template. It will build on your Word document itself, keeping its styles, headers, document control and the ten-screen structure. Each screen section starts with short numbered steps and a marked screenshot, then your reference tables follow.

Where your template and today's demo site disagree, the guide follows the demo. The seat lists each difference for you, for example if the question or category counts have changed. The test with an agent that has never seen the system still has to pass.
Received. From now on, decisions I need from you go on the dashboard under fleet activity. I'm finding exactly where that section is fed from, then I'll post the open ones there.

Done. The 11 HPSM-POC decisions are now cards under Fleet activity, each with my recommendation and what happens if you don't answer. From now on, every decision I need from you goes there as a card.

The two that unblock the most: send the Playbook PowerPoint, and register the Azure providers.
Received: the cards landed on Tuesday's board, not Friday's. I'll pick up your replies from Tuesday's board for these 11, and I'm fixing it so future cards go to the Friday board.

You're right, the cards went to Tuesday's tab. The board chooses the tab from the project name, and Datasec means Tuesday, even though my cards are stored as Friday's. I've fixed the page, and Wednesday is deploying it because the live board is hers.

Once it's live, the cards move to the Friday tab on their own, and your taps there come straight to me. Until then, Tuesday will forward any answers you give on her tab. I've also saved the lesson: check what you actually see, not just the tool's success message.

Received: five more HPSM-POC documents, including the screen image set, a SOW, the developer design document, the financial model and the 7-slide deck. I'm filing them, checking which ones we already have, and passing anything new to the build seats.

Kam, I can't see your answers on Tuesday's tab. My seat is locked out of the Datasec partition on purpose, for client isolation. I asked Tuesday at 11:39 to forward them to me, and nothing has arrived yet.

The quickest fix is to paste your answers here in one line, card name and letter each. For example: rs11 a, pdf-library a, branch-protection a.

If you'd rather wait, I'll act on them as soon as Tuesday's forward lands, or once Wednesday deploys the board fix and the cards show on this tab.
Received: the Playbook PowerPoint, v3. I'm filing it and pulling out the 16 questions now.

Kam, one thing needs your hands: registering the 9 Azure providers. Paste this into a terminal:

export AZURE_CONFIG_DIR="/Users/kamilkreiser/1FILES TO SYNC/HPSM-POC/4_Credentials/.azure"; for ns in Microsoft.CognitiveServices Microsoft.Web Microsoft.Sql Microsoft.KeyVault Microsoft.Storage Microsoft.Insights Microsoft.OperationalInsights Microsoft.ManagedIdentity Microsoft.AlertsManagement; do az provider register -n $ns; done

Everything else you ruled is done. Main now needs a pull request with green CI, and I read the settings back to confirm. The Entra API app exists, with you as Admin and no secrets. The private backup repo exists, and Seat A pushes the analysis documents to it.

Your deck has the real 16 questions. They're the partner readiness self-assessment on slide 99: tick boxes, the score is the count ticked, and there are four bands with a 30-day plan for each. The seats are building from the deck's exact wording.

Two new cards on the Friday tab: whether to use checkboxes as in the deck or the four-option scale from the mocks, and your two not-applicable answers, which point opposite ways.
Received. When the Composer user guide is finished and has passed the test with a fresh agent, I'll email you the Word and PDF versions at kamil.kreiser@datasec.com.au.

The Composer user guide for Paul is in your inbox at kamil.kreiser@datasec.com.au. It came as two emails, PDF and Word, because together they were too large for one. Before you forward it, three quick cards on the Friday tab. The demo shows an HP SOW file name on its control pages, and so do the screenshots. The font is HP Forma, from your template. And four test engagements are left on the demo.

On HPSM-POC, the readiness PDF report is merged and main is green. The web pull request is on its second and last fix round, for a mobile layout that is 12 pixels too wide on Linux fonts.

Received: once you've answered a card, I'll take it off Fleet activity. I'm clearing the 11 you've already answered now, and I'll do the same with every answer from here on.
Done. The 11 cards you've answered are now off Fleet activity. Only the ones still waiting on you remain. From now on, a card disappears as soon as I record your answer.
Received. I'll email you the v1.2 guide at kamil.kreiser@datasec.com.au once it passes the salesperson test and I've reviewed it.

You can unplug the Spark. Nothing is using it right now: no open connections, and no seat holds its lock. The only seats running are the two Composer ones, and that project has no local-model setup. When you plug it back in, I'll restart the model and the connection before the next HPSM-POC round.

Kam, only part of the Spark shutdown worked. I stopped the model and closed my connection to it, so it's safe to unplug now. But powering the box off needs its admin password, which I don't have.

If you'd rather shut it down cleanly first, run this in a terminal and enter the box's password when asked:

ssh -t ZGX-Nano-G1n sudo shutdown -h now

Or just hold the power button.
